text.p: Iomega Corp said on Thursday that the disk-drive manufacturer had a "challenging" quarter with its gross margins as aggressive price cuts on its products offset cost reductions.
In a conference call with analysts, Chief Executive Officer Kim Edwards said gross margins for the third quarter fell to 26.3 percent from 26.9 percent in the second quarter.
Edwards also said sales of Iomega's disk drives in the U.S. and the Far East were better than planned at $259 million. Iomega lumps U.S. and Far East sales together in its results.
European sales in the quarter fell to $51 million from $56 million a year ago because of sluggish PC sales and a new management, Edwards said.
Earlier Iomega reported third quarter profits rose to $12.8 million from just over $2 million in the year ago period.
